clue.text: Steal out of it with as little as possible.

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase; the answer as an adverb means to the smallest degree

indicators.note: someone out of it is confused and disordered, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: Advice to a thief: take only the bare minimum when you pilfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steal' looks like the definition but is the fodder: 'out of it' rearranges its five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb the word means to the smallest extent, the tiniest amount one can manage.

clue.text: Manufacturing rifles shouldn't get out, possibly.

definitions.note: describes the people themselves: those who perhaps ought never to be released

indicators.note: manufacturing makes something new out of raw material, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A worry that a gun factory's secrets might leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manufacturing' looks like the subject, but it signals an anagram of RIFLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners serving life sentences are, perhaps, people never to be released from jail.

clue.text: They might be fastened with a tie or snap, but poorly so.

definitions.text: They might be fastened with a tie

indicators.note: done poorly means badly arranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Garments fastened by a tie or a press-stud, but not securely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly' signals an anagram of OR SNAP; 'with a tie' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen pinafores are typically held on by strings knotted behind the back.

clue.text: The people who collect taxes, but not yours or mine?

parts.note: the IRS is the Internal Revenue Service, the US tax-collecting agency

explanation.surface: A grumble that tax collectors take money that is not really their own.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nation is an American paper, so the taxman is the IRS.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun for a third party's property is what belongs to other people, neither you nor me.

clue.text: Might it hang around you unfortunately?

definitions.text: Might it hang around you unfortunately?

parts.words: Might it hang around you unfortunately?
parts.note: the seabird hung round the Ancient Mariner's neck in Coleridge's poem, now a byword for a burden of bad luck

explanation.walkthrough: In The Rime of the Ancient Mariner the sailor who shot the bird must wear its body round his neck, so the creature became an emblem of a curse you carry.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of a bird round one's neck names a persistent burden or source of misfortune.

clue.text: People with money, as they say, might be ineffectual toys.

definitions.text: People with money, as they say

indicators.note: these letters could be turned into something else if rearranged, which marks an anagram

explanation.surface: A jibe that rich people are like toys that do nothing useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might be' says the letters of INEFFECTUAL TOYS could become something else when rearranged. 'As they say' marks the definition as a stock phrase, coined by J. K. Galbraith in 1958.
explanation.definitionFit: Galbraith's term describes a wealthy nation in which most citizens enjoy prosperity.

clue.text: The typical Englishman? Something to beat, with the doctor about on the case of a famous detective.

parts.note: the British bulldog is the emblem of stubborn English character
a drum is beaten

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go around the next word

parts.note: MD is Doctor of Medicine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quintessential Englishman with a drum and a doctor on a famous detective case.
explanation.walkthrough: The British bulldog is the national emblem of stubbornness. 'About' wraps the doctor round 'on' for MOND. The hero is Sapper's 1920s gentleman adventurer.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Hugh Drummond, nicknamed after a dog breed, is the investigating hero of popular British thrillers and films.

clue.text: Part of the engine connected with the choke?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the valve that controls fuel flow to an engine

explanation.walkthrough: 'Choke' looks like the car part next to the engine, but it is the verb to strangle.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuel valve in a motor and the act of strangling share this one word.

clue.text: After going to the middle of the circle, any progress must be.

definitions.text: After going to the middle of the circle, any progress must be.

parts.words: After going to the middle of the circle, any progress must be.
parts.note: once you are at the centre of a circle, every direction leads away from it

explanation.walkthrough: From the centre there is nowhere further in to go, so any movement heads away towards the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in a direction away from the centre, as every path from the middle of a circle must.

clue.text: Dentures might, but they're not permanent measures.

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: false teeth fill gaps in a mouth
second meaning: temporary fixes until something better comes

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer in two to read the first sense: false teeth plug holes in a smile.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift arrangement meant to serve only until a proper solution arrives is this kind of measure.

clue.text: Patterned rug of felt, but you might not remember it so.

definitions.text: you might not remember it so
definitions.note: an adjectival description: the state in which one fails to remember

indicators.note: something patterned has its parts laid out in a new design, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A rug made of felt with a design so dull it slips from memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patterned' seems to describe the rug, but it tells you to rearrange RUG OF FELT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent-minded who fails to recall things is in this state, so the description fits the adjective.

clue.text: It might be proportionate with it, or a form of it.

definitions.text: It might be proportionate with it

indicators.note: a form of something is a version of it in another shape, so these letters are recast in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about something being in proportion to itself, or a variant of itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' signals an anagram of OR A plus the final 'it'; the opening 'It' is the answer, the relation two proportionate quantities share.
explanation.definitionFit: Proportionate quantities keep a fixed relationship between them, and that fixed relation is expressed as a quotient.

clue.text: Given this, there's evasion of what some dogs do to track.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: being given this treatment means being dodged and fobbed off

definitions.text: what some dogs do to track
definitions.meaning: second meaning: greyhounds literally race round a track, which is the phrase read as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: Racing greyhounds circle an oval course, so the two words read literally; as a noun the same phrase means evasive treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: To get this from someone is to be deceived or kept waiting with excuses instead of a straight answer.

clue.text: It might take pluck to make it, unless it's part of the speech.

definitions.text: It might take pluck to make it
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the vibrating note sounded by plucking a string
second meaning: a nasal or regional accent in someone's voice

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' looks like courage, but it means plucking a guitar string; 'part of the speech' sounds like grammar but means an accent.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the ringing sound of a plucked string and a distinctive nasal accent in a voice.

clue.text: Sort of unplugged after a point, but got close.

indicators.note: the anagram comes after the compass point in the answer

parts.note: S is south, one of the compass points

indicators.note: sort as a verb means arrange, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone pulls the plug on a gadget and then moves nearer to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' looks like 'somewhat' but makes NUGGLEDUP, which goes 'after' S; the 'point' is a compass point, not a dot or a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle up against someone is to cuddle in tight beside them.

clue.text: A mugwump is beyond his intellect, by definition.

definitions.text: A mugwump is beyond his intellect, by definition.

parts.words: A mugwump is beyond his intellect, by definition.
parts.note: a joke definition calls a mugwump a person schooled beyond his intellect

explanation.walkthrough: Mugwump is American slang for a self-important independent, especially in politics; a popular gibe defined him as schooled beyond his intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Being schooled and learned is what the word means; the gibe says the mugwump has more schooling than brains.

clue.text: Is around comparatively tardy, but shuts off.

indicators.note: the two letters of Is wrap around the phrase that follows

parts.note: taken as written
so late: tardy to such a comparative degree

explanation.surface: Someone who is later than others keeps shutting things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comparatively tardy' gives SO LATE (tardy to such a degree), and 'Is around' puts I...S around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarantine or cut someone off from others is to set them apart, the same as shutting them off.

clue.text: One of those agents tidying things up in McLean serves to make it obvious.

definitions.text: One of those agents tidying things up

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters McLean serves, spanning the two words

parts.note: the letters run from inside McLean into serves, across the word break

explanation.surface: A detergent in a place called McLean whose job is to make dirt plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To make it obvious' only adds that the answer is plain to see once spotted in the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent or soap is a substance used to remove dirt, one agent of tidying.

clue.text: It might reveal the record to look certain.

parts.note: a record is a gramophone disc
lo is an old exclamation meaning look
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A device that might show what is on a record so you can check it properly.
explanation.walkthrough: LO, as in 'lo and behold', is the crossword stock word for look.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation of a secret is an act that makes something known, the noun form of revealing.

clue.text: Instant importance?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a very brief period of time
second meaning: significance, as in a matter of great weight

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that two unrelated senses share one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a split second of time and weight or consequence.

clue.text: Iron, for example, starting in the sixties or seventies.

definitions.text: Iron, for example, starting in the sixties or seventies.

parts.words: Iron, for example, starting in the sixties or seventies.
parts.note: the Iron Age is one example of an age, and the later one of a person's life begins at sixty or seventy

explanation.walkthrough: Iron is an example of an age (the Iron Age); the sixties look like the decade but are a person's years.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stage of life, when people grow elderly, is usually reckoned to begin at sixty or seventy.

clue.text: Brushes off a chance to make some money on a bet?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cleans away with a broom

definitions.text: a chance to make some money on a bet
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a sweepstake, a gamble where the pooled stakes go to the winner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brushes off' looks like dismissing someone; here it is clearing dust with a broom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both clearing with a broom and a short name for a lottery-style betting pool.

clue.text: Jonson asked her to drink to him, after a fashion.

definitions.text: Jonson asked her to drink to him, after a fashion.

parts.words: Jonson asked her to drink to him, after a fashion.
parts.note: Ben Jonson's poem addressed to this woman begins 'Drink to me only with thine eyes'

explanation.walkthrough: 'After a fashion' is because she is asked to drink only with her eyes, not with a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1616 lyric by Ben Jonson is titled with this woman's name and opens with that famous toast.

clue.text: It doesn't mean one which is often passed — descriptive of certain marriages.

definitions.text: It doesn't mean one which is often passed
definitions.meaning: first meaning: unwritten law built from court precedent, as opposed to a statute that a legislature passes
second meaning: a couple living together as spouses without a ceremony

explanation.walkthrough: Statutes are laws that get passed; the answer is the body of law that grew from judges' decisions instead, so it does not mean a passed law.
explanation.definitionFit: A union recognised by long cohabitation rather than a wedding is described with this adjective, after the unwritten legal tradition.

clue.text: Carries from set to set in a better way.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lugs things about, as stagehands haul props between sets
second meaning: the tote, the totalisator, is the way a better (one who bets) places a wager

explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is one who bets, not 'superior': the tote is the pool-betting system at a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: To lug something is to haul or transport it, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Is it clear it's formerly a single set price?

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
a single thing is one
a rate is a fixed charge

explanation.surface: A shopper asking whether a fee that used to be one fixed price is now transparent.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone of blame is to absolve them, the legal sense of the verb.

clue.text: What Shiva did, reputedly.

parts.note: in Hindu belief Shiva is the Destroyer in the trinity with Brahma the Creator and Vishnu the Preserver

explanation.walkthrough: Shiva's role in the Hindu trimurti is to bring the universe to an end so it can be remade.
explanation.definitionFit: The god known as the Destroyer is said to have wrecked and dissolved worlds, the past tense of that work.

clue.text: Is prolific with sides, by the sound of it.

indicators.note: tells you the word for sides is said aloud and a word that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: sides in a game are teams

explanation.surface: Someone is fertile with ideas for picking sides, or so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To swarm or abound with something is to be full to overflowing, a fit for being prolific.
